compatibility_badge: PCB Layout Change Required (Pinout or Package Mismatch)

pin_diff.note: CRITICAL OUTPUT STAGE DIFFERENCE: LM2903DR is comparator (open-collector) vs LM358DR2G opamp (push-pull); a comparator is an uncompensated open-loop switching device (no internal Miller/dominant-pole compensation) and will oscillate or latch in a linear negative-feedback op-amp circuit, while an op-amp used as a comparator suffers slow saturation/overdrive recovery and propagation delay far worse than its slew rate implies; the open-collector/open-drain output can only sink current and requires an external pull-up resistor to reach logic-high, whereas the push-pull output actively drives both rails (a pull-up tied to a different rail can back-drive a push-pull stage).
Functionally identical IN_NEG_A pin (1IN- vs Input A-).
Functionally identical IN_POS_A pin (1IN+ vs Input A+).
Functionally identical VEE pin (GND vs VEE/Gnd).
Functionally identical IN_POS_B pin (2IN+ vs Input B+).
Functionally identical IN_NEG_B pin (2IN- vs Input B-).

CRITICAL OUTPUT STAGE DIFFERENCE: LM2903DR is comparator (open-collector) vs LM358DR2G opamp (push-pull); a comparator is an uncompensated open-loop switching device (no internal Miller/dominant-pole compensation) and will oscillate or latch in a linear negative-feedback op-amp circuit, while an op-amp used as a comparator suffers slow saturation/overdrive recovery and propagation delay far worse than its slew rate implies; the open-collector/open-drain output can only sink current and requires an external pull-up resistor to reach logic-high, whereas the push-pull output actively drives both rails (a pull-up tied to a different rail can back-drive a push-pull stage).

parameter_matrix.note: Op-amps (internally compensated for linear feedback) and comparators (uncompensated open-loop switching) are NOT drop-in interchangeable.
Single SOT-23-5 op-amps vary in pin ordering across vendors; verify Pin 1–5.
A part wins only if its recommended Vs range strictly encompasses the counterpart on both ends.
Exceeding Vs,abs causes immediate gate-oxide or junction breakdown.
Closed-loop -3 dB bandwidth scales as f_-3dB = GBWP / Acl.
Controls large-signal full-power bandwidth SR / (2π·Vpeak) or comparator switching speed.
Lower Vos minimizes DC error in current-shunt and sensor bridge amplifiers.
CMOS/JFET pA-class inputs avoid offset voltage drops across high-impedance (>100 kΩ) sensors.
Multiply by channel count for total IC standby current draw.
RRIO prevents clipping on low-voltage 3.3 V single-supply ADC buffers.
Winner requires superiority on both CMRR (higher) and input voltage noise (lower); mixed tradeoffs stay CONTEXT.
Important when driving heavy resistive loads or high supply rails.

swap_risks: CRITICAL OP-AMP VS COMPARATOR TRAP: LM2903DR is a comparator with open-collector output while LM358DR2G is a opamp with push-pull output. Even with identical pinouts, a comparator is an uncompensated switching device: dropping it into a linear negative-feedback op-amp circuit (buffer, gain stage, filter) causes oscillation or latch-up, and an op-amp used as a comparator suffers slow overdrive/saturation recovery. In addition, the open-collector/open-drain output requires an external pull-up resistor to swing high.
HIGH THERMAL MARGIN: Package θJA is 43% higher on LM358DR2G (LM2903DR: 148.5 °C/W p.5 vs LM358DR2G: 212 °C/W p.3); re-check Tj = Ta + Pd × θJA against Tj,max.
HIGH MINIMUM SUPPLY FLOOR: LM358DR2G requires Vs,min >= 3 V (p.1) vs 2 V on the counterpart; confirm low-battery / brown-out operation still clears the higher floor.

HIGH TEMPERATURE GRADE MISMATCH: Rated ambient range differs (LM2903DR: -40..125 °C Extended Industrial (-40°C to 125°C) vs LM358DR2G: 0..70 °C Commercial (0°C to +70°C)); LM358DR2G cold limit only 0 °C, LM358DR2G hot limit only 70 °C — verify product ambient qualification before swapping.
engineering_verdict: LM2903DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and LM358DR2G (onsemi, SOIC-8) are NOT drop-in interchangeable (Level 3 PCB Layout / Circuit Change Required) due to device kind mismatch (comparator/open-collector vs opamp/push-pull) — circuit redesign required. Specific pin conflicts: Pin 1 (OUT_A vs OUT_A), Pin 7 (OUT_B vs OUT_B). Signal-chain deltas: comparator (open-collector) vs opamp (push-pull), supply ceiling 30 V (p.4) vs 30 V (p.4), Vos 7 mV (p.10) vs 7 mV (p.4), Ib 2x gap (25000 vs 45000 pA). Primary bench gotchas to watch: LM2903DR "Extended -40°C to +125°C Upgrade Over LM393DR, But Wider Offset (7 mV / 15 mV Over Temp)" (p.10) and LM358DR2G "CRITICAL ESD Trap: Standard onsemi LM358DR2G Is Rated ONLY 250 V HBM / 100 V MM (p.3)!" (p.3). BOM decision: Choose LM2903DR when the circuit is an open-loop threshold/window comparator (open-collector output); choose LM358DR2G when the circuit is a linear closed-loop amplifier, buffer, or active filter. Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.1) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
